member.name: T:WizardWrx.HTTP.JSON_Deserialized_Object
member.summary: Instances of this class provide a lightweight, schema-aware façade over a JSON payload. The class optionally sanitizes the input, validates required fields, and exposes a minimal set of typed accessors so callers can retrieve field values without depending directly on JSON.NET, working with JToken instances, or needing to expend the effort to parse the JSON into a strongly-typed model when only a few fields are needed.

remarks.para: The typed getters intentionally cover only the canonical .NET types that map cleanly and unambiguously to JSON: string, Boolean, 32-bit integer, double-precision floating point, Guid, and DateTime. JSON does not define numeric widths, temporal subtypes, or alternative Boolean representations, so additional getters (such as byte, short, long, float, DateOnly, DateTimeOffset, or truthy/falsy coercions) would not provide meaningful additional capability. Callers who require more specialized interpretations can retrieve the raw string value and apply domain-specific parsing rules.

This design keeps the API surface minimal, deterministic, and intention-revealing, while insulating callers from JSON.NET and preserving the ability to evolve the internal representation in the future.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.JSON_Deserialized_Object.GetFieldValueAsBoolean(System.String)
member.summary: Query the JSON object for a specific field and attempt to parse it as a Boolean.
member.param: This string represents the name of the field for which to check.
member.returns: The return value is a nullable Boolean representing the value of the field, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as a Boolean.
member.remarks: JSON has a native Boolean type, and JSON.NET preserves it directly, so this accessor returns true or false only when the underlying token is a JSON Boolean or a string that .NET recognizes as a Boolean literal (“true” or “false”, case-insensitive). JSON.NET does not coerce other string values to Boolean, and the .NET framework does not define truthy/falsy semantics for values such as “yes”, “no”, “0”, or “1”. Callers who require more flexible Boolean interpretation should retrieve the raw string and apply domain-specific rules.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.JSON_Deserialized_Object.GetFieldValueAsDateTime(System.String)
member.summary: Query the JSON object for a specific field and attempt to parse it as a DateTime.
member.param: This string represents the name of the field for which to check.
member.returns: The return value is a nullable DateTime representing the value of the field, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as a DateTime.

remarks.para: This method provides the canonical double precision floating point number accessor for this class.

This method retrieves the field value as a DateTime. Since JSON has no native date or time type, and date values are represented as strings. This method parses those strings using , which is sufficient for ingestion scenarios where the exact original offset is not required and the primary goal is to obtain a usable DateTime value.

A DateTimeOffset getter is intentionally omitted because JSON does not guarantee the presence or meaning of timezone offsets, and callers who require offset-preserving semantics can parse the raw string explicitly using .

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.JSON_Deserialized_Object.GetFieldValueAsDouble(System.String)
member.summary: Query the JSON object for a specific field and returns its value as a double, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as a double.
member.param: This string represents the name of the field for which to get the value. The method will attempt to parse the value of this field as a double.
member.returns: The return value is a nullable double representing the value of the field, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as a double.

remarks.para: This method provides the canonical double precision floating point number accessor for this class.

JSON numeric values are represented internally as doubles, and every valid float value is also representable as a double. Because double is strictly a superset of float in both range and precision, there is no scenario where a separate GetFieldValueAsFloat method would return a meaningful result that this method cannot.
Callers who require a float can cast the returned double value.

remarks.para: This method retrieves the field value as a Guid, which is a common representation for identifiers in many JSON-based systems. JSON has no native Guid type, so values are stored as strings and parsed here using .

Additional identifier getters (such as UInt64 or custom ID formats) are intentionally omitted, since callers with domain-specific identifier requirements should interpret the raw string according to their own rules.

member.name: M:WizardWrx.HTTP.JSON_Deserialized_Object.GetFieldValueAsInt(System.String)
member.summary: Query the JSON object for a specific field and return its value as an integer, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as a 32-bit signed integer.
member.param: This string represents the name of the field for which to check.
member.returns: The return value is a nullable integer representing the value of the field, or null if the field does not exist or cannot be parsed as an integer.

remarks.para: This method provides the canonical integer accessor for this class.

This method retrieves the field value as a 32-bit integer. JSON does not define distinct numeric widths, and JSON.NET represents all integer tokens internally as Int64. This method returns the value only when it fits safely within the range of Int32. Smaller integer types (byte, short) are subsets of Int32 and do not require separate getters, since callers who need them can cast the returned value.

A 64-bit integer getter is intentionally omitted because JSON does not guarantee that numeric values fall within the precise range of Int64. Callers who require 64-bit semantics should parse the raw string explicitly, using .

remarks.para: This method provides the canonical string accessor for this class.

JSON string tokens map directly to .NET strings, and JSON does not distinguish between different textual subtypes (such as char, multiline text, or encoded binary). Additional getters for narrower textual types would not add meaningful capability, since callers who require a more specific representation can interpret or validate the returned string as needed.

returns.para: This routine was originally intended for use as part of a library that interacts with the Microsoft Graph API and expects to return an arbitrarily shaped object as a JObject, which it passed to the callback routine .

Since it is being pulled out of that class library so that it can be applied elsewhere, it is changed so that it returns whichever object it has, either JSON or an ordinary string. Hence, altough the return type is specified as object, in practice, it is either a JObject or a garden variety String.

The OAuth token expired and a replacement cannot be obtained from the Microsoft Azure identity server.
Another type of exception arose while processing a request against the Microsoft Graph API endpoints.
